name: Life Sciences
title: Clinical study deviation evidence assembly
summary: Assemble protocol deviation evidence for study teams while preserving source records and qualified reviewer decisions.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A clinical study operations team receives visit exceptions across sites, laboratory feeds, and electronic data capture. Reviewers need to distinguish missing data from a potential protocol deviation and document their assessment. The agents assist records management and operational review, not participant care or trial eligibility decisions.
problem: Protocol amendments differ by site activation date, and late lab results can change the evidence available at review. Flattening these timelines into a summary risks applying the wrong requirement or implying a clinical conclusion unsupported by source data.
whyAgents: Specialists independently align protocol versions, reconcile visit events, gather approved source references, and assemble the review packet. Their separation supports explicit evidence ownership and prevents a drafting agent from amending captured clinical observations.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Evaluate preparation effort together with source traceability and reviewer correction frequency. The proposed architecture does not establish regulatory compliance; study owners must map their actual procedures, systems, and oversight requirements before deployment.

agents.name: Protocol version agent
agents.responsibility: Determine the applicable approved protocol and site activation interval.
agents.boundary: Cannot interpret clinical exceptions or change approved requirements.

agents.name: Visit reconciliation agent
agents.responsibility: Compare scheduled and recorded visit events with source timestamps.
agents.boundary: Cannot modify case report forms or impute missing observations.

agents.name: Laboratory evidence agent
agents.responsibility: Match incoming results to permitted study subjects and visits.
agents.boundary: Cannot assess participant safety or recommend treatment.

agents.name: Deviation packet agent
agents.responsibility: Draft the chronology, conflicting evidence, and reviewer questions.
agents.boundary: Cannot classify final deviation severity or submit external reports.

systems.name: Clinical data capture platform
systems.role: Authoritative captured observations, queries, and correction history.

systems.name: Study and protocol management systems
systems.role: Supply site assignments, approved amendments, and effective activation dates.

systems.name: Laboratory and quality systems
systems.role: Provide specimen events and controlled review records without granting model write access to source evidence.

flow.title: Register exception
flow.description: Create a study-scoped event using subject pseudonym, site, visit, and source revision; preserve the original signal.

flow.title: Resolve protocol interval
flow.description: Match the site's activation history to the event date and expose unresolved amendment applicability for reviewer attention.

flow.title: Reconcile chronology
flow.description: Compare scheduled visits, collection timestamps, receipt timestamps, and late corrections without conflating their meanings.

flow.title: Collect evidence
flow.description: Retrieve the minimum permitted study records and build a provenance manifest that points back to controlled originals.

flow.title: Draft assessment packet
flow.description: Describe the possible deviation, missing evidence, and contradictory facts; reserve clinical significance and final classification for qualified reviewers.

flow.title: Record disposition
flow.description: Save the approved assessment with reviewer identity and source versions; subsequent source corrections reopen dependent review sections.

failures.scenario: A site activation date is missing for an amendment.
failures.detection: Protocol interval resolver cannot select one valid version.
failures.recovery: Block protocol comparison and assign the unresolved date to study operations before drafting conclusions.

failures.scenario: A laboratory result arrives after the packet was signed.
failures.detection: Source event version advances for an evidence item linked to the assessment.
failures.recovery: Notify the responsible reviewer, preserve the signed record, and open a linked amendment assessment.

controls: Use study pseudonyms in prompts and isolate reidentification mappings from agent access.
Enforce site and study entitlements on all source queries and exports.
Preserve source records and corrections; agent drafts never overwrite captured observations.
Require qualified review of deviation classification and any participant-impacting decision.
Record amendment version, site activation interval, and evidence cutoff in every packet.

metrics.name: Evidence traceability
metrics.definition: Reviewed packet assertions with resolvable controlled source references divided by audited assertions.

metrics.name: Version resolution rate
metrics.definition: Exceptions with unambiguous applicable protocol versions divided by all registered exceptions.

metrics.name: Review preparation time
metrics.definition: Elapsed time from exception registration to reviewer-ready chronology, segmented by site and event class.

metrics.name: Reopened assessment rate
metrics.definition: Assessments reopened for late or corrected evidence divided by completed assessments.

tradeoffs.cost: Requires accurate site activation metadata and correction procedures.
Some reconciliation work must remain in a separately authorized service.
Late evidence requires linked amendments rather than convenient overwrites.

rollout.acceptance: Reviewers validate amendment selection and chronology on representative exceptions with known dispositions.
One study permits draft packets after pseudonymization, source access, and correction-history tests pass.
Approved dispositions enter the quality system only after late-evidence reopening and audit reconstruction are demonstrated.
